claim: Mail is fast, but it cannot interrupt a turn; long worker turns and ended sessions produce the whole tail.

metric.what: Created-to-read time per message from the mail store, by route.

countedFrom.machine: one Windows 11 machine; one master, 8 orchestrators, about 50 short-lived workers, one person
versions: agent harness as installed in the period (exact version not recorded)

proposedChange: Workers run long jobs in the background so turns stay short. A send to a session with no live process fails loudly. Document that an unread message usually means mid-turn, not idle.
whyItGeneralises: Mail between sessions that cannot interrupt a turn has a tail set by turn length on any fleet; the created-to-read measure is fleet-independent.
